name: Macrophagic Myofasciitis

criteria.description: Presence of macrophage aggregates with PAS-positive cytoplasmic inclusions in muscle biopsy
Chronic diffuse muscle pain and fatigue persisting for more than 6 months
History of intramuscular aluminum-containing vaccine administration prior to symptom onset
MRI showing muscle edema and fascial inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of macrophage aggregates with PAS-positive inclusions plus chronic muscle symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires muscle biopsy; clinical and vaccination history support diagnosis but are not definitive alone.

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Normal or mildly elevated creatine kinase (CK)
imaging: MRI showing muscle edema and fascial inflammation
other: Muscle biopsy showing macrophage aggregates with PAS-positive cytoplasmic inclusions
History of aluminum-containing vaccine administration at biopsy site

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of rimmed vacuoles on muscle biopsy
Lymphocytic infiltration on muscle biopsy without macrophage aggregates
Absence of inflammatory infiltrates on biopsy
Widespread pain without objective muscle pathology

redFlags: Severe dysphagia or respiratory muscle involvement
Unexplained high fever or systemic symptoms
references: Gherardi RK, Coquet M, Chérin P, et al. Macrophagic myofasciitis lesions assess long-term persistence of vaccine-derived aluminum hydroxide in muscle. Brain. 2001;124(Pt 9):1821-1831.
Authier FJ, Chérin P, Payré B, et al. Macrophagic myofasciitis: characterization and pathophysiology. Lupus. 2006;15(7):452-457.
Couette M, Authier FJ, Gherardi RK. Macrophagic myofasciitis: an emerging entity. Curr Opin Rheumatol. 2007;19(6):591-598.
